research_rationale: EO 6249 approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Lace Manufacturing Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, subject to one condition creating a Lace Manufacturing Industry Committee as a planning and fair practice agency. Both operative clauses (the approval and the committee condition) depend on the code approval power in NIRA section 3. Following the reviewed shared NIRA analysis, the first end is the statutory repeal by S.J. Res. 113 on 1935-06-14; Schechter (1935-05-27) is a validity characterization only; 1935-06-16 is not an end. Held text is an APP mirror transcription: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.
savings_reason: Acts, liabilities and complying action under the approved code before 1935-06-14 are accrued effects; the section 5 antitrust exemption for completed action under an approved code is accrued, and the proviso of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle its reach. Nothing continues the approval or the committee condition after the repeal.
earlier_end_check: The order's own text states no period, until-date or provisional approval; the only dates are the 1933-08-14 signing and a recital of code submission. A search of held order texts for the code name and this order's number found no revocation, cancellation, suspension or superseding code before 1935-06-14; amendments to the code would be later events, not ends. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935, and June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.
scope_check: The lead clause says "is hereby approved, subject to the following condition:" and approves the amended Lace code under Title I; clause (1) is a condition of that approval creating a Lace Manufacturing Industry Committee to cooperate with the Administrator. Machine inventory of two clauses (lead and (1)) was checked against the full text and is complete; the recitals and the Administrator's recommendation/signature block command nothing.
independent_command_check: Clause (1) is a condition attached to the approval, to effectuate the policies of the act through a planning and fair practice agency under the code; it rests on Title I and no other statute, so it is not an independent command and falls with the approval. The order makes no appointment, delegation or other direction outside the code approval.
savings_check: Section 5 of the NIRA exempts any code "approved, prescribed, or issued and in effect" and complying action while Title I is in effect and sixty days thereafter; this is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this order. No held source continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

research_rationale: EO 6606-E (1934-02-17) amends the first condition of the President's earlier approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Electrotyping and Stereotyping Industry (the approval of December 23, 1933), substituting a revised hours/work-sharing condition and a local Fact Finding Board and Labor Board appeal procedure, and publishes a statement on how that condition is to be read. The held text supports two clauses, both resting on the code approval power in NIRA section 3 (the machine inventory had one clause covering only a mid-text fragment and omitted the published statement). Following the reviewed shared NIRA analysis, the first end is the statutory repeal by S.J. Res. 113 on 1935-06-14; Schechter is a validity characterization only. Held text is an APP mirror transcription: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.
savings_reason: Acts, liabilities and complying action under the code and its amended condition before 1935-06-14 are accrued; the section 5 exemption for completed action is accrued, and the held proviso names agreements and states no time limit. Nothing continues the amended condition after the repeal.
earlier_end_check: The order states no period, until-date or provisional term. A search of held order texts for the code name and this order's number found no revocation, cancellation, suspension or superseding code before 1935-06-14. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935, and June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.
scope_check: Clause 1 is the amendment: it orders that the earlier approving order "be and it is hereby amended accordingly", substituting the revised first condition of approval (sections (a) through (e) on the local Fact Finding Board and the Labor Board appeal). Clause 2 is the published statement that the condition is not to be construed to conflict with section 7(a) of the Act. The machine inventory (one clause of characters 2542-3877) was corrected to these two spans covering the whole operative text.
independent_command_check: Both clauses alter or construe a condition of the code approval and rest on Title I; the order also cites authority "and otherwise" without naming another statute or making any appointment or delegation, so no clause is independent of the code approval. The Administrator's recommendation and signature block command nothing.
savings_check: Section 5 of the NIRA exempts any code "approved, prescribed, or issued and in effect" and complying action while Title I is in effect and sixty days thereafter; this is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this order.
